stories.name: Kyle Larson clinches his third NASCAR Cup Series championship
facts: At the season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday, Nov. 8, Kyle Larson (Hendrick Motorsports, No. 5 Chevrolet) clinched the 2026 Cup Series title by finishing fourth in Stage 1, which ended under caution after Chase Briscoe's engine failure.
Larson finished the race 12th and won the title by 49 points over Christopher Bell; Ryan Blaney won the race, passing Tyler Reddick on the last lap.
It is Larson's third Cup title and second in a row, making him the first back-to-back champion since Jimmie Johnson. Crew chief Cliff Daniels and team owner Rick Hendrick celebrated atop the pit box.

people.name: Cliff Daniels
people.verified_action: Celebrated atop the pit box and radioed Larson that they had won (NBC Sports, Heavy). Drawn atop the pit box with a headset, arms raised; generic team shirt, no logos.

people.name: Rick Hendrick
people.verified_action: Celebrated atop the pit box and radioed congratulations (NBC Sports). Drawn beside Daniels with white hair, arms raised; generic, no logos.

stories.visual_notes: High-angle view over a pit box at Homestead-Miami: in the foreground two team figures celebrate on top of the pit box, while beyond them the field circles in a single file behind a yellow pace car under caution, with Larson's No. 5 mid-pack. Radio arcs link the pit box antenna to the car. Palm trees, grandstands and a bright South Florida afternoon sky. No text besides the car number, no trophy, no race-winner depiction.
stories.confidence: high: NBC Sports and Heavy Sports (independent, both read in full, both published Nov. 8) agree on the Stage 1 clinch, the 12th-place finish, Blaney's win and the third title; Wikipedia's cutoff-safe Nov. 8 events list (citing AP, which could not be fetched) matches. Larson's car livery is not verified, so it is drawn generically.
